sample_walkthrough_title: Understand a complete app through samples.
sample_walkthrough_intro: Follow the samples source through directory structure, the application entry, URL mapping, Route attributes, Request-Type, languages, configuration, templates, forms and database operations. Each chapter includes code, source files and relevant demos.
sample_layout_intro: samples separates public files, configuration and application code. The repository root vendor/autoload.php loads the framework and plugins; SlightPHP uses samples/app as its application directory.
sample_layout_public: www is the document root and contains index.php and static assets. config holds routes and application settings; app holds controllers, templates, language catalogs and page data. Configuration and templates stay outside the public directory, with compiled templates in the system temporary directory.
sample_layout_modules: Site serves the website, Workspace handles tasks, Lab contains routing, template and language experiments, and Widgets contains reusable modules. Organize new controllers by namespace and templates in matching folders. Keep page content and code snippets in app/data.
sample_routing_intro: Default paths map /directory/controller/method. Register short URLs with Route::set() or load rules with Route::setConfigFile(). samples registers PHP rules first, then appends rules from routes.json.
sample_routing_mapping: /workspace/main/entry maps to Workspace\MainController::Entry() in app/Workspace/MainController.php. The custom /r/hello route maps to /lab/route/entry/hello; $request->route contains the full route while $request->get holds ?source=examples separately. routes.json adds /tasks, /tasks.json and multiple-parameter routes. The first registered matching rule wins.
sample_routing_methods: Route attributes still apply after URL mapping: Api allows GET, Save allows POST, and the route lab allows GET and POST. A mismatch produces 405 with Allow. Save also uses #[Route(csrf: true)]; the app checks permissions.
sample_language_intro: app/languages contains one folder per locale. main.json holds interface messages; demo.json holds the language experiment messages. Set the directory and locale, then call Language::tr(key, zone) to read a message.
sample_language_selection: The entry calls SampleI18n::boot(), choosing a valid lang parameter, then the saved cookie, browser Accept-Language, and finally zh-cn. Set the locale before the first translation. The fixed zh-cn above demonstrates the API; the actual controller uses the language already chosen by the entry.
sample_language_catalogs: Maintain keys in zh-cn, zh-tw and en. Language returns translated text; the application replaces {name} using strtr. Templates use SampleI18n::t() and Tpl handles encoding; PHP that outputs HTML directly must still escape it. User input stays raw, and missing translations fall back to the original key.
sample_templates_intro: The entry configures template paths, compiled files and default { / } delimiters. Every template escapes by context by default; the lab runs all modifiers, JS/CSS, include/part, template comments, literal and cache examples.
sample_templates_composition: include shares the current instance; part uses its module template instance. The automatic examples run raw, escape, default, tr, tostring and version, plus HTML, URL, JS and CSS encoding.
sample_templates_config: The development demo disables Config’s process cache. Cached long-running processes do not automatically check file modification times; handle cached settings or restart workers after changes.
sample_database_intro: Use the task scenario to add MySQL storage to your own deployment. This site still uses sessions; the schema and database snippets below are an extension and do not execute on this page. Prepare MySQL, PDO and pdo_mysql, create the database and table, then add samples/config/db.json.
sample_database_setup: Replace the sample database, account and CHANGE_ME with your connection settings. Keep db.json outside www and supply real credentials through deployment. Db::setConfigFile() selects the file; useConfig("tasks") opens the main connection in the tasks section. Check that the connection succeeds.
sample_database_binding: insert(table, item) creates a row; select(table, condition) reads rows; update(table, condition, item) changes them; delete(table, condition) removes them. Associative arrays bind condition and field values. Keep table and column names fixed by the application. This example updates and deletes only its newly inserted task.
sample_database_results: insert returns the new ID; select returns Db\Data with rows in items; update and delete return affected row counts, where zero can be valid. Failures return false, so check with === false. The framework does not retry automatically. For atomic operations, use begin(), commit() and rollback() on the same connection and check their results.
sample_database_integration: To integrate this with the workspace, add app/Model/Task.php to wrap the operations. Have tasks() read the database and Save() write it, preserving method checks, CSRF and 303 redirects. A multi-user application also needs an owner field and owner checks on every read, update and delete; this minimal schema illustrates the API.
sample_request_type_intro: The same /lab/type/entry URL calls Entry() without a type header and ajaxEntry() with Request-Type: ajax. This controller runs in samples and returns plain text identifying the selected method.
sample_request_type_dispatch: Allowed prefixes default to page, ajax, part, json, xml and html, configurable with SlightPHP::setAllowRequestTypes(). An allowed Request-Type prefixes the entry name; missing or unlisted values use the unprefixed entry. fetch does not add Request-Type automatically.
sample_request_type_guard: Visiting /lab/type/ajaxentry without Request-Type returns 405. Request-Type is independent of GET or POST; both Entry methods have GET-only attributes. Type rejections have no Allow header; HTTP method mismatches return Allow: GET. Neither replaces permissions or CSRF checks.
sample_request_type_try_intro: Send real GET requests and compare the results with no type header, an ajax header and a direct prefixed-method URL.
sample_request_type_ready: Choose a request to inspect its status and response body.
sample_request_type_nojs: Enable JavaScript to use these buttons, or run the fetch snippet in browser developer tools.
sample_forms_intro: The task form posts title, action and _csrf, using a token from Csrf::token(). The dispatcher validates #[Route(csrf: true)] before constructing the controller; Save() then validates and handles the business operation.
sample_forms_validation: Route(method: POST) restricts the HTTP method. A failed #[Route(csrf: true)] check throws an exception, which the entry maps to 403. Titles must be strings with 1–80 characters after trimming, with at most 50 tasks. Browser required and maxlength attributes help users, while server validation runs independently.
sample_forms_redirect: After processing, a 303 redirect returns to the list and a flash message shows the result. Refreshing reads the list without repeating the submission. The excerpt comments stand for the full method’s validation and task update steps.
sample_request_failed: The request failed. Check your connection and try again.
sample_entry_intro: samples/www/index.php is the public entry point. It loads Composer from the repository root, boots language settings, sets the app directory and extracts a path without the query string from REQUEST_URI. The excerpt shows initialization.
sample_entry_dispatch: The default zone, page and entry are site, main and entry, so / dispatches to Site\MainController::Entry(). Controllers live under appDir. The entry configures the environment; controllers handle individual pages.
sample_entry_errors: After initialization, the entry loads route rules and calls SlightPHP::run(). It outputs returned strings and catches dispatch exceptions to produce 404, 405 or error pages, with Allow where appropriate.
sample_route_methods_intro: Add a PHP 8 #[Route(...)] attribute to a public entry to restrict HTTP methods. These excerpts from Lab\TypeController show GET-only Entry and GET/POST Preview, both returning plain text.
sample_route_methods_syntax: Import SlightPHP\Route. Use #[Route(method: "GET")] for one method or #[Route(methods: ["GET", "POST"])] for several, immediately before the method declaration. Without the attribute, this HTTP restriction does not apply.
sample_route_methods_rejection: A mismatch throws METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED before constructing the controller. The samples entry returns 405 with the allowed methods in Allow. POST to Entry returns 405 and Allow: GET; GET and POST to Preview both return 200.
sample_route_methods_dispatch: Route::set() maps URLs, #[Route] restricts HTTP methods, and #[Route(csrf: true)] validates Session tokens. After Request-Type selects a prefixed entry, attributes on the actual method apply. Workspace Save() uses Route with POST and csrf: true; the app still checks identity and permissions.
sample_route_methods_try_intro: Send GET and POST to both entries and inspect the status, Allow header and selected method. These demos only return text.
sample_config_intro: samples/config/example.json stores the application name, flags, task limit and features. Workspace Plugins() reads it with Config::getConfig() and passes it to a template. Configuration stays outside the document root at an application-defined path.
sample_config_values: JSON objects become objects, accessible as $config->application->name. Arrays, numbers and booleans retain their types. getConfig($file, "application") reads a section directly; $application->limit accesses its limit.
sample_templates_output: Pass raw data. Modifiers transform it before encoding for the output context. A final raw marks trusted content. Cached JS plans avoid lexical rescanning. The compile directory must be writable; render() outputs directly.
tpl_demo_intro: The outer page and independent module both escape by context by default. The templates execute the displayed code and results.
tpl_demo_modifier_note: Defaults, translations, debug text and versions transform data first. escape avoids duplicate encoding; a final raw marks trusted output.
tpl_demo_javascript: JS values, strings, template strings, regexes and events
tpl_demo_js_pending: Enable JavaScript to see the executed result.
tpl_demo_event_button: Write the sample text on the right
tpl_demo_default_delimiters: Default {} delimiters, dollar signs and literal
tpl_demo_comments_note: Use the default { / } delimiters and write comments as {* ... *}. Single-line and multiline template comments are removed during compilation. Their assignments and HTML never execute or render, so the result stays VISIBLE. Comment syntax inside literal is displayed verbatim. Comments end at the first *}, cannot nest, and throw InvalidArgumentException if left unclosed.
tpl_demo_cache_note: The same template receives <FIRST> and then <SECOND>. The cache stores a plan, not frozen data. JS is analysed when compiling the plan; a new dynamic entry compiles a variant once and later hits skip lexical scanning.
tpl_demo_rejection_note: The controller catches each isolated example error and discards that render output. Tpl still throws normally while the page displays the result.

csrf_demo_form_intro: The form sends the current token in the hidden _csrf field. Success redirects here with 303, so refreshing does not repeat the submission.
csrf_demo_form_saved: Form validated. One submission was recorded.
csrf_demo_ajax_intro: Ajax reads content from the _csrf meta tag generated by tokenMeta() in the page head and sends it as X-CSRF-Token. Compare valid, missing and invalid tokens. JSON body fields are not used for CSRF validation.
csrf_demo_ready: Choose a request to see its actual HTTP status.
csrf_demo_rejected: CSRF validation failed. The submission count did not increase.
csrf_demo_nojs: Enable JavaScript to compare Ajax requests. The HTML form and token rotation work without JavaScript.
csrf_demo_rotate_intro: Open this page in another tab, then rotate the token here. Submitting from the old tab returns 403; reload that tab to continue. Old task workspace forms in this session also expire.
csrf_demo_rotated: Token rotated. Reload old forms in other tabs.
csrf_demo_custom_intro: Set csrf to --csrf--token for the form field, meta name and request header. Ajax reads the token from that meta tag. The default _csrf and X-CSRF-Token do not apply to this entry.
csrf_demo_two_forms: Three equivalent options: write the field with token(), assign HTML from tokenInput(), or call tokenInput() directly in Tpl. Use |raw when outputting the complete HTML tag.
csrf_demo_direct_intro: Call the static method in the template without assigning csrf_input first. It reads the current session token during rendering; |raw outputs the complete hidden tag.
lab_ready: Run an example to see the result here.
lab_not_ready: Required dependencies or service configuration are not ready.
lab_setup: See this guide for dependencies and service configuration.
lab_failed: Run failed. Check service connectivity, permissions, dependencies or network. Internal error details are hidden.
lab_upload_note: Displays only the name, size and PHP upload error code. Files are not saved. Server upload limits apply.
lab_json_note: JSON does not populate post. This example parses getContent() and sends the token in X-CSRF-Token.
lab_cookie_read: Read the sample cookie from a new request
lab_captcha_code: Enter the lowercase letters in the image
lab_http_note: Calls a fixed httpbin echo service with a five-second timeout. GET sends query parameters, POST sends JSON, and 404 demonstrates an upstream exception.
lab_nojs: Forms and response links work without JavaScript. JSON buttons and inline response previews require JavaScript.
lab_footer: This page calls the actual plugins. Configure external services as described in the guide.
lab_intro_config: Read real JSON / JSONC files and inspect types, the whole configuration and missing-zone fallback.
lab_intro_log: Choose a level and format, write to a temporary log and read its actual content. The temporary file is then removed.
lab_intro_db: Run a parameterized SELECT inside a transaction, then roll it back. Requires MySQL configuration; this example does not create or modify tables.
lab_intro_redis: Write a unique sample key, read its value and TTL, then delete it and inspect the result. Keys expire after 30 seconds.
lab_intro_http: Send real upstream requests using Guzzle and inspect the body, headers and exception status.
lab_intro_error: Call an error or exception handler explicitly and read a temporary log. The page retains its normal response and displays the output as text.
lab_intro_captcha: Generate a real captcha image and validate it in this session. A successful check consumes it; refreshing replaces the previous answer.
lab_intro_request: Inspect query parameters, forms, upload metadata, JSON bodies, headers and routes. Only sample data is displayed.
lab_intro_response: Inspect real statuses and headers, compare write / end, and test cookies and a 303 redirect.
lab_request_card: Request snapshots: query parameters, forms, files, headers and raw bodies.
lab_response_card: Send statuses, headers, cookies, bodies and redirects.
lab_request_need: The framework creates Request / Response. Set headers before writing the body.
lab_session_card: Start native sessions on demand, update data by reference and read the session name and ID.
lab_session_need: Requires ext-session; configure the name, cookies and cache policy before first use.
lab_intro_session: Submit text to save it in this browser session and increment the counter. Refresh to read the saved data, or use another browser session to compare isolation. The session ID is not displayed.
